name: Sahar Basin
notes: Locked palette: 36 ramp colours, which is the set all rendered sprites are quantized to in CI. Ramps are ordered light -> dark. Reserved bands MUST NOT appear in unit/building/terrain diffuse art; they are applied at runtime by the VFX and team-color systems only.

limestone.role: primary terrain, masonry, concrete, sun-bleached surfaces
limestone.note: Interpolated to twice the original resolution. Nine warm steps across limestone+dust could not carry lit stone: quantizing a building render banded it and pushed mid-tones into gunmetal and olive. Every original entry is retained, so sprites quantized against the narrower ramp are still on-palette. Endpoints and hues are unchanged -- this is more resolution, not a new art direction.

dust.note: Interpolated to twice the original resolution. Nine warm steps across limestone+dust could not carry lit stone: quantizing a building render banded it and pushed mid-tones into gunmetal and olive. Every original entry is retained, so sprites quantized against the narrower ramp are still on-palette. Endpoints and hues are unchanged -- this is more resolution, not a new art direction.

terracotta.role: fired roof tile, parapet coping, trim bands on masonry
terracotta.note: Added for the building set. The reference architecture bands every parapet and coping in fired red, and the warm ramps could not carry it: limestone and dust are desaturated tans, and the only red-orange in the palette was vfx.ember, which is reserved and must stay contrast-safe against fire. Three steps is enough for a band, its shadow, and its underside -- a tile roof does not need a ramp as deep as a wall.

skin.note: Added for the infantry overhaul. The art brief calls for visible skin, and no existing entry could carry it: the warm ramps are ochre rather than rosy, so a face rendered on dust.2 quantized into terracotta and read as blood spatter. Chosen by searching plausible skin HSV for maximum distance from the existing 42 -- these sit 33 from dust.2, their nearest neighbour, which is the same separation terracotta already lives with, and 41 from each other so a face has light and shadow rather than one flat patch. Two entries, not three: a face is about six pixels at gameplay zoom.

shadow.role: cast shadow, occlusion, interiors, night base

grass.role: procedural terrain only -- open sward, hedgerow, pasture. NOT for sprite art.
grass.note: Added for the Naharin green basin. Neither existing green could carry open ground: olive is a desaturated grey-green for hulls and tarps, and scrub is two entries whose declared role is sparse vegetation. Five steps of 39-43 RGB distance, coarser than limestone's ~31 because five entries span what nine limestone steps span. The ramp stops at grass.4 (#6E9E33) rather than continuing down, because scrub.0 (#6B8A4A) is 31 away and already owns that band -- extending further produced duplicates, not steps. Vegetation is therefore seven steps across two ramps: grass.0-4 then scrub.0 then scrub.1. grass.2 is the open-ground wash: its luminance (177) sits within 5 of limestone.3 (182), which every unit silhouette was tuned for figure-ground against, so the change is hue and not value.

vfx.role: RUNTIME ONLY. Saturated band reserved so explosions and tracers pop against desaturated terrain. Rejected by CI if found in static art.

team.role: RUNTIME ONLY. Applied via palette remap on masked pixels. Author team-color regions in pure magenta #FF00FF in the source .blend material.

group.role: RUNTIME ONLY. Control-group badge and selection ring, indexed by group slot 1-9. Never appears in static art.
group.note: Nine hues separated around the wheel and held light enough that the badge's #14150F numeral stays legible at gameplay zoom. g1 keeps the lime the badge always used, so existing muscle memory survives. Deliberately avoids team.hostile, vfx.fire and team.neutral at close range: those already mean enemy, suppression and neutral on the same unit, and a badge that borrows them reads as state rather than membership.
